kind: assumed inputs and analysis choices; nothing in this file is measured in the Demerzel repository

rounding.note: Every stored ratio is an exact fraction of integers, rounded once when it is written.

quantile_rule: nearest rank: the p% quantile of n values sorted in increasing order is the value at position ceil(p * n / 100)
median_rule: the middle value of the n values sorted in increasing order; when n is even, the mean of the two middle values (the nearest-rank 50% quantile would take the lower of the two)

episodes.note: Analysis choice, taken from PSY-008 so that both lessons name the same groups: a burst day has at least burst_day_from events (PSY-008's threshold, above the 99% quantile of its Poisson benchmark), and burst days at most gap_days apart belong to one episode.

checkpoints.note: Analysis choice: the dates at which the mean and the median 'to date' are read, the last day of each calendar month and the last day of the log.

day_boundary_offsets_hours.note: Analysis choice. The lesson counts days in UTC; each offset recounts them with the day boundary moved by that many hours (the local date of a clock set to UTC plus the offset).

type_subsets.note: Analysis choice: the same measures on the events of one group of types, over the same calendar days.

capacity.note: Assumed handling rule, applied to the observed daily counts and to the synthetic logs. The consumer these triggers were written for was never scheduled (observed-input.json, design), so no row computed from this rule is a measurement of the project.
capacity.handling_rule: Each day, after the day's arrivals, at most `capacity` events are handled, oldest first. Events that are not handled wait for the next day. Capacity that is not used on a day is lost. The wait of an event is the number of days between its arrival day and the day it is handled (0 = handled on its arrival day).
capacity.wait_tolerance_note: The design's staleness limit (72 hours, observed) read at the fixture's one-day resolution: an event is late when it is not handled within 3 days of its arrival day. An event still waiting on the last day is late if those 3 days have run out, and undetermined otherwise.

plans.rule: the mean number of events per calendar day, rounded up to a whole event

plans.rule: nearest-rank quantile of the daily counts

plans.rule: nearest-rank quantile of the daily counts

plans.name: p99
plans.rule: nearest-rank quantile of the daily counts

capacity.earlier_readings_note: Every plan above is sized on the same days it is then run on, which no planner can do. To show what that hindsight is worth, each plan is also sized on the days read up to each date of `checkpoints` except the last, then run on the days that follow, starting with an empty queue (which favours the plan).

hand_case.note: Worked by hand in the README; analyze.py asserts each expected value.

poisson_control.note: Synthetic logs with the observed number of events and of calendar days and no concentration beyond chance: every event falls on a day chosen uniformly at random, independently of the others. This is a homogeneous Poisson process conditioned on its total.
poisson_control.generator: rng = random.Random(seed); for each log, for each event: day = min(days - 1, int(rng.random() * days))

replication_tolerance.note: Self-check that can fail: the two batches must agree on these batch means within these absolute differences.

empty_days_tolerance.note: Known-answer check of the generator: the batch mean of the number of empty days must be within this distance of the exact expectation days * ((days - 1) / days) ** events.

hand_computed_cases.note: Worked by hand in the README; analyze.py asserts each expected value with three formulas for the Gini coefficient.

candidate_logs.note: Imaginary summaries used by one exercise: logs with the observed number of events and days, described only by two measures. Neither exists.

transfer_task.note: Hypothetical support desk for the learner task: tickets opened per day over two weeks. Not Streeling data and not a forecast.

plans.rule: the mean number of tickets per calendar day, rounded up to a whole ticket
